# dsh-lfaa
English | 中文
A complete native DSH plugin project with independently owned business modules. Appearance, layout,
cards, dialogs and motion are one capability group, not the definition of the whole plugin. This is
a new project designed around DSH; it does not copy or migrate the old LFAA project.
DSH owns accounts, all AI execution, sessions, models, subagents, tool dispatch and approval. The pl
ugin contributes its own business through public interfaces and keeps business data local when neede
d. No second harness, login or conversation store is introduced.
The three-column writing workspace manages novel projects and chapters, autosaves the selected chapt
er, and sends AI polish/continuation prompts through a selected DSH conversation. Results appear as
suggestions and are applied only after a user action. Writing data is stored locally under the verif
ied DSH account profile ID.
## Repository

Package directories and manifest names use the `dsh-` prefix. Private implementation packages are bu
ndled into one installable `dsh-lfaa` artifact; users do not install the development workspace.
## Develop
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The DSH repository root is also an install facade: its manifest points to the committed `dist/packag
es/dsh-lfaa/` output, so GitHub installs do not need to run a build lifecycle script. The package sh
ips both root entries and matching `dist/` compatibility entries for older DSH loaders. In DSH's Add
Plugin dialog, enter the repository URL `https://github.com/yubboo/dsh-lfaa.git`; for a local insta
ll, run `pnpm run build` first and enter this repository's root directory. The GitHub push menu rebu
ilds the installable output before staging it. The build excludes private workspace dependencies, de
velopment source, test fixtures and user data. The package name `dsh-lfaa` works after the built dis
tribution is published to npm. On Windows, run `publish-npm.bat` from the repository root: menu 6 sa
fely pushes to GitHub `main`, requiring a commit message that starts with a new three-part source ve
rsion; menu 7 builds, previews and publishes to the official npm registry after confirmation, and me
nus 1–5 provide package checks. The last pushed source version is read from GitHub commit history, w
ith a local Git config fallback. The menu implementation is `scripts/publish-menu.ps1`; the batch la

Minecraft currently supports Paper and Fabric Host services and Agent operations, with a session wor
kspace panel for distribution/version discovery, server create/install, status, start/stop, configur
ation, file inspection, console commands, backup/restore, and mod search/install. Fabric mods are se
arched through Modrinth by Minecraft version and installed only into a stopped Fabric instance; requ
ired dependencies are resolved recursively and downloaded files are checked against Modrinth SHA-512
metadata. Modpacks, Forge, NeoForge, and end-to-end acceptance in a real DSH Profile remain unfinis
hed. The panel submits explicit requests into the active DSH conversation; the Agent inspects Java a
nd may install an official Temurin runtime when needed, while downloads, writes, and process actions
remain subject to DSH approval. The user must explicitly confirm Minecraft EULA acceptance. Paper d
ownloads carry publisher SHA-256 metadata. Fabric's official HTTPS bootstrap endpoint does not publi
sh the same checksum metadata, so the plugin records the downloaded file's local hash and validates
its JAR format without claiming publisher-checksum verification.
